name: Creamed spinach
summary: Chopped spinach softened with onion and folded through a smooth, nutmeg-scented white sauce, the green side no South African Sunday roast is without.
about: Creamed spinach is a fixture of the South African Sunday lunch, beside roast chicken or lamb, butternut and rice. Local cooks make it with the big-leaved Swiss chard sold as spinach in every supermarket.
steps: Cut the thick white stalks out of the spinach and slice the leaves into thin ribbons.

Put the wet leaves in a large pot over medium heat, cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring once, until wilted and bright green. Tip into a colander, press out as much water as you can with a spoon, then chop finely on a board.
Melt the butter in the same pot over medium heat and fry the onion until soft and see-through, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then add the warm milk a little at a time, stirring constantly, until you have a smooth sauce. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, still stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the spinach, cream (if using), nutmeg, salt and pepper and heat through for 3 minutes, until hot and creamy. Serve straight away.
prepNote: Make up to a day ahead and reheat gently with a splash of milk; it also freezes well.
